name: Data Freshness Card
summary: A metric card that knows how old its number is. It shows the age, marks the figure stale and then 'last known', keeps the last good value beside a failed refresh, pauses while the tab is hidden or offline, and computes age from timestamps so a background tab cannot make it lie.

attempts.prompt: Build a metric card that shows its value, how long ago it was updated, and announces changes to screen readers.
attempts.problem: The status sentence carried the age, and it lived in a polite live region. During a failed refresh it read 'Showing the value from 41 seconds ago', so a screen reader was handed a new sentence every second for as long as the error stood. The visible age has to tick; the announcement has to change only when the state does.

attempts.prompt: Mark the figure as stale with a badge, and show offline state in the footer.
attempts.problem: The badge came out as uppercase monospace with letter-spacing, and the footer read 'Offline · measured 2 minutes ago' with a middle dot — both patterns this site's design system bans, the first because uppercase labels shout, the second because a dot-separated meta string is a template tell. Neither is a bug; both made the card look generated.

finalPrompt:
Build a React + TypeScript + Tailwind metric card that never presents an old number as current. No dependencies.

Show a label, the figure in tabular numerals, and when it was measured: "Updated 8 seconds ago" in a <time datetime> with the exact clock time as its title. Compute the age from the measurement timestamp on every render, never by counting down: background tabs throttle timers to a minute or less, and a counter returns from a hidden tab claiming an hour-old figure is seconds old.

Three states from age alone. Fresh below staleAfter. Stale from staleAfter: the figure dims and a plain lowercase badge says "stale". Expired from expireAfter: the badge says "last known", because the figure is no longer a claim about now.

Refresh with a button and optionally on an interval:
- While a refresh is in flight the card is aria-busy, the button is disabled and says "Refreshing…", and the old figure stays visible. Never blank a number to show loading.
- A failed refresh keeps the last good figure and puts the failure directly under it, in a role=alert line that says what failed and how old the shown figure is. Not a toast, not a replaced card.
- Pause the clock and the interval while document.hidden, and while offline. Say "Offline" in the footer and disable refresh. Coming back visible or online with a stale figure refreshes at once.

One polite live region gives one sentence per change of state: updated, stale, out of date, refresh failed. Never include the ticking age in it, or a screen reader hears a new sentence every second.

Under reduced motion, the refresh icon does not spin and the colour change does not transition. No uppercase labels, no middle-dot meta strings. Props: label, initialValue, initialAge, fetchValue, formatValue, unit, staleAfter, expireAfter, autoRefresh, refreshLabel, disabled, onRefresh, onError, onFreshnessChange, className. Colours from tokens only.
why:
A dashboard number is a claim that something is true now, and nothing about it in a screenshot says whether the claim still holds. That is the invisible behaviour: what the card does as time passes, and what it does when it cannot find out. A model asked for a stat card produces the number and a refresh button, and the figure looks exactly as authoritative an hour later as it did when it loaded.

The timestamp rule is the one worth stating with its reason. A countdown is the obvious implementation, it works in every demo, and it lies the first time someone comes back to a tab they left. Computing age from the measurement time costs nothing and cannot drift.

The live-region bug is a quieter version of the same mistake: putting a value that changes every second into a channel that is read aloud on change. The visible text and the announced text have different jobs, and the prompt has to say which is which.
